candidate.blueprint_locator: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control, printed p.8/PDF p.12
candidate.blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — HAI surveillance
candidate.educational_objective: Explain the role of standardized NHSN definitions in consistent HAI surveillance and trend monitoring.

options.A: To allow each unit to redefine an infection whenever local rates increase
options.B: To replace clinical diagnosis and treatment decisions for individual patients
options.C: To apply consistent surveillance criteria so infection events and trends can be measured comparably over time
options.D: To count every positive culture automatically as a health-care-associated infection

candidate.rationale: NHSN surveillance uses standardized event definitions and criteria so facilities can identify reportable surveillance events consistently and trend data over time. Surveillance definitions are not substitutes for individual bedside diagnosis.
candidate.source_claim_supported: NHSN standardized definitions support consistent surveillance event identification and trend measurement.
candidate.source_document_title: NHSN Patient Safety Component Manual — Bloodstream Infection Event Protocol
candidate.source_locator: 2026 BSI protocol — NHSN surveillance definitions and criteria; CDC surveillance recommendation III.B
candidate.source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) / National Healthcare Safety Network (NHSN)
candidate.stem: Why does a health-care facility use standardized CDC/NHSN surveillance definitions when tracking health-care-associated infections over time?
